verdict.rationale: GitHub's docs say anyone can fork a repository to create a new repository on GitHub (github-docs-68, github-docs-50). They also describe the pull request workflow for proposing and reviewing code (github-docs-69), with PR review available on mobile and the CLI (github-docs-71, github-docs-75). The core fork-and-propose loop is clearly delivered, but the evidence never explicitly ties the two together. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of opening a pull request from a fork back to the upstream repository, maintainer controls for outside contributors (e.g., allowing edits from maintainers), and independent or hands-on corroboration.
